previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, COPD, obstructive sleep apnea, diastolic heart failure, and tobacco use was admitted for acute hypoxic respiratory failure. She presented with worsening dyspnea and altered mental status due to severe hypercapnia. Initially managed with non-invasive ventilation, she required intubation due to respiratory fatigue. Treatment included mechanical ventilation, broad-spectrum antibiotics later narrowed to levofloxacin for presumed pneumonia, systemic steroids for COPD exacerbation, and aggressive diuresis for acute on chronic heart failure. Bronchoscopy and cultures showed no bacterial or viral pathogens. She was extubated after four days, transitioned to supplemental oxygen, and started on inhaled fluticasone-salmeterol. Acute kidney injury developed from over-diuresis but resolved with fluid repletion. She improved steadily, regained independence in breathing, and was discharged to extended care with home oxygen, smoking cessation support, and follow-up plans.

She is discharged on lasix 100 mg daily, with instructions to 
have her BMP checked early next week to monitor potassium and
